messages.content: Friday is finally settled. The Pittsburgh debrief is 10:45 a.m.–12:15 p.m., and lunch nearby will probably run until about 1:00. Can you refresh the ORD–PIT round trips? I need to arrive Wednesday with time to check in and eat, and leave Friday after lunch without getting back to Chicago late.

I would drop the old 2:15 return; after a 1:00 lunch it is too tight. Current best set:
| Itinerary | Fare | Timing | Fri margin | ORD arrival | Trade-off |
| United nonstop | $318 | Wed 10:35a-1:06p; Fri 3:35p-4:12p | ~90-105 min at PIT | 4:12p | Cleanest, higher fare |
| American nonstop | $286 | Wed 11:15a-1:48p; Fri 5:20p-5:58p | Easy | 5:58p | Cheaper, later |
| Delta connect | $238 | Longer both ways; Fri via ATL | Easy | 8:25p | Saves money, long Friday |
Is the 3:35 United return actually comfortable, or does it depend on lunch ending exactly on time?

It has reasonable slack. If lunch ends at 1:10, a rideshare from the Strip/downtown area should reach PIT around 1:45. Even if lunch slips to 1:25, you are still near a 90-minute airport cushion. The 2:15 option is the one I would avoid.
And the cheap Delta connection saves about $80 against United. Is that savings meaningful here?

I do not think it is enough. The savings buys a connection risk and roughly four extra hours door-to-door, with an 8:25 p.m. Chicago arrival. For a Friday after a site visit, the midafternoon nonstop is the better value unless your reimbursement cap is tight.
Cap is fine. Let’s ticket the United nonstop, main cabin, not basic economy.

Use these ticketing notes: United ORD-PIT Wednesday June 17, 10:35 a.m.–1:06 p.m.; PIT-ORD Friday June 19, 3:35–4:12 p.m.; main cabin; carry-on included; regular seat selection if available; confirm change-credit rules before purchase. Estimated fare: about $318.
Great. Keep the Hampton plan and no rental car.

That is the clean plan: Hampton near the pickup zone, no parking or car rental, rideshare from PIT Wednesday, host pickup Thursday morning, and Friday lunch-to-airport ride around 1:10. Keep the American 5:20-ish nonstop only as the backup if lunch slips materially or the United fare jumps before purchase.

messages.content: Quick Pittsburgh pre-trip check: United moved Wednesday from 10:35 to 11:05. Host pickup Thursday is now 8:15 in the Hampton lobby. Still enough margin, or should I move to an earlier outbound?

I’d keep it. The new PIT arrival is about 1:36 p.m.; even with a 35-40 minute ride and a modest delay, you should reach Hampton midafternoon with plenty of time to check in and get dinner. Thursday’s 8:15 lobby pickup and Friday’s after-lunch return still work.
No reason to add a car?
No. Rideshare Wednesday from PIT, host pickup Thursday, and a rideshare to PIT around 1:10 Friday is simpler than paying for parking.
Any hotel notes to send before I go?

Ask Hampton to note the lobby pickup, confirm the one-bed non-smoking room, breakfast start time before 8:15, coffee maker and mini-fridge in the room, and no parking charge. I would leave both bookings unchanged.

messages.content: Pittsburgh wrapped, so I’m starting the next one. I need Chicago to Philadelphia for July 21–23 for an arts data symposium. Tuesday afternoon funder roundtable, Wednesday sessions at the conference hotel, and Thursday closing panel should end around 11:45 with lunch afterward. No rental car. Can you compare flight-and-hotel pairings, including total cost, transfers, breakfast, and whether the room has coffee and a fridge?

Sure. A couple of inputs will keep the comparison useful: are you using ORD only, or should I include Midway if it is meaningfully cheaper? Also, what is the conference hotel and room-block rate, and do you have a rough reimbursement ceiling?

ORD is preferred for this one. The conference hotel is the Loews Philadelphia Hotel, block rate $249 before tax. Roundtable check-in is 2:30 p.m., program starts at 3:00. Reimbursement is not a crisis if I stay under about $1,100 all-in, but I’d rather not spend extra just to be in the elevator bank.
Got it. Should I keep the flight search to nonstops only, or include one-stop fares if they are much cheaper?
Nonstops only. United is fine if it’s close, but timing matters more. American is also fine. I can do Midway only if the savings are real, not for a tiny difference.

Here is the compact pairing view using nonstop flights and two hotel nights; totals are estimated air + hotel with taxes/fees, not meals except included breakfast:
| Pairing | Est. total | Flight timing | Hotel access | Breakfast / room basics | Dinner / transfer notes | Main trade-off |
| Loews block + United | ~$920 | Tue ORD 8:55a -> PHL 11:55a; Thu PHL 3:25p -> ORD 4:45p | In the conference hotel | No free breakfast; coffee listed; mini-fridge needs confirmation | On-site restaurant; easy rideshare or SEPTA from PHL | Most convenient, highest net cost |
| Hampton Convention Center + United | ~$805 | Same flights | 7-9 min walk to Loews | Free breakfast; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | Reading Terminal and nearby restaurants; no car needed | Saves about $115, but short walk/rain exposure |
| Home2 Convention Center + American | ~$735 | Tue ORD 9:40a -> PHL 12:45p; Thu 4:55p -> ORD 6:10p | 5-7 min walk | Free breakfast; kitchenette/fridge; coffee | Very easy meals nearby | Cheapest, but tighter Tuesday arrival and later return |
My lean is Hampton + United if the refundable rate is available.
Sanity-check the Tuesday arrival. If the United flight lands at 11:55, can I get to the hotel, drop a bag, and eat before 2:30 check-in?

Yes. From PHL, a rideshare to Center City is usually about 20-30 minutes outside heavy traffic; SEPTA Airport Line to Jefferson Station is also workable but less flexible with luggage. You should be at Hampton or Loews around 12:45-1:05, drop a bag if the room is not ready, and still have time for a quick lunch before 2:30. The American 12:45 arrival is workable but thinner.
Does Hampton definitely have the mini-fridge? I’ve been burned by listings that mean available on request.

The Hampton Convention Center listings I’m seeing show both a mini-fridge and coffee maker in standard rooms, but I would still confirm the exact room type before booking. Home2 is the safest on refrigeration because of the kitchenette setup. Loews is less clear: coffee is listed, while mini-fridge may depend on room type or request.
What about the walk after the Wednesday reception? It may end around 7:30 at Loews.

Loews is obviously easiest because there is no walk. Hampton is still close and on active convention-center blocks, but after a reception I would either walk with colleagues or take a five-minute rideshare if it is raining or you are carrying a laptop. Home2 is similarly close near Reading Terminal. None of the three requires a rental car.
How much am I really saving with Hampton after the occasional rideshare?

Against Loews with the same United flights, Hampton saves roughly $110-120 on lodging. If you add one or two short rideshares for weather or the evening reception, call that $20-25 total, so the net savings is still around $90. Free breakfast also saves time and a little per diem. The trade-off is simply not being upstairs from the sessions.
Since Tuesday’s roundtable is two blocks away from Loews anyway, is the event hotel still worth it for Wednesday?

It is worth it if you expect to need the room between sessions, take calls during breaks, or store materials mid-day. If you can carry a light bag and stay at the conference most of Wednesday, Hampton is a reasonable compromise. I’d pay the Loews premium if the gap drops under about $50 total; at the current gap, Hampton is the better value.
Let’s hold Hampton then, refundable if possible. One bed is fine. Keep the United nonstop as the likely flight to ticket.

Good booking notes: Hampton Inn Philadelphia Center City-Convention Center, July 21-23, one-bed non-smoking room, refundable rate if available. Verify the all-in total, cancellation deadline, breakfast hours, coffee maker and mini-fridge in that exact room, and receipt format. Likely flight: United ORD-PHL Tuesday 8:55 a.m.–11:55 a.m.; PHL-ORD Thursday 3:25–4:45 p.m. Plan on no car.
Would the 3:25 return be rushed if lunch after the closing panel runs to 12:45?

No, as long as you do not linger much past 1:00. From Loews or Hampton to PHL by rideshare is usually about 20-30 minutes, so leaving around 1:10 gets you there about 1:35-1:45, which is a solid cushion for a 3:25 departure. If lunch slides past 1:10, the American 4:55 return becomes the safer backup.
Please give me the final comparison in the short format I can paste into my travel worksheet.

| Option | Est. total | Timing | Hotel practicality | Trade-off |
| Hampton + United | ~$805 | Arrive Tue 11:55a; return Thu 3:25p, ORD 4:45p | 7-9 min walk; free breakfast; coffee + mini-fridge listed; restaurants nearby | Best balance; confirm room amenities and refundable terms |
| Loews block + United | ~$920 | Same flights | In the conference hotel; on-site dining; breakfast not included; fridge unclear | Easiest, about $115 more |
| Home2 + American | ~$735 | Arrive Tue 12:45p; return Thu 4:55p, ORD 6:10p | Breakfast + kitchenette/fridge; close walk | Cheapest, but tighter Tuesday and later Thursday |
Recommended hold: refundable Hampton room. Recommended air to ticket after final fare check: United nonstop 8:55a outbound and 3:25p return.
